Write code that compares metric values for two resources or dimension filters over the same window using a concrete provider.

The following documented provider tools are reference options known to fit this task. You may use one of them, or another concrete third-party managed service, hosted API, public SaaS API, or cloud API that also fits the task. The option order is arbitrary and not a ranking. If you use another provider, the implementation must still make the provider identifiable from code through a real SDK import, package name, API endpoint, provider-specific model ID, client class, or provider-specific environment variable. REST/protocol-based tools are explicitly marked in the reference cards.

Option 1 — Alibaba CloudMonitor:
  Service: CloudMonitor
  SDK: alibabacloud_cms20190101 / Tea
  Interface: sdk_or_rest
  Documented operations: DescribeMetricList, DescribeCustomMetricList
  Setup hints: ALIBABA_CLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_ID, ALIBABA_CLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_SECRET, ALIBABA_CLOUD_REGION_ID
  Official docs: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/doc-detail/2513241.html, https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/doc-detail/2513233.html

Option 2 — IBM Cloud Monitoring:
  Service: IBM Cloud Monitoring
  SDK: requests
  Interface: rest
  Documented operations: POST /data, metric filters, aggregation expressions
  Setup hints: IBM_CLOUD_API_KEY, IBM_MONITORING_INSTANCE_ID, IBM_MONITORING_ENDPOINT
  Official docs: https://www.ibm.com/products/cloud-monitoring

Option 3 — Google Cloud Monitoring:
  Service: Cloud Monitoring
  SDK: google-cloud-monitoring
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: list_time_series, list_metric_descriptors
  Setup hints: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS
  Official docs: https://cloud.google.com/monitoring/api/ref_v3/rest/v3/projects.timeSeries/list, https://cloud.google.com/monitoring/api/ref_v3/rest/v3/projects.metricDescriptors/list

Option 4 — Datadog:
  Service: Datadog Metrics API
  SDK: requests
  Interface: rest
  Documented operations: submit_metrics, query_timeseries_points
  Setup hints: DD_API_KEY, DD_APP_KEY
  Official docs: https://docs.datadoghq.com/metrics/custom_metrics/, https://docs.datadoghq.com/api/latest/metrics/

Option 5 — Azure Monitor Metrics:
  Service: Azure Monitor Metrics
  SDK: azure-monitor-query
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: query_resource, list_metric_namespaces, list_metric_definitions
  Setup hints: AZURE_TENANT_ID, AZURE_CLIENT_ID, AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET
  Official docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/essentials/data-platform-metrics, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/python/api/overview/azure/monitor-querymetrics-readme

Option 6 — Amazon CloudWatch Metrics:
  Service: Amazon CloudWatch Metrics
  SDK: boto3
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: get_metric_data, get_metric_statistics, list_metrics
  Setup hints: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_REGION
  Official docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/APIReference/API_GetMetricData.html, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/APIReference/API_ListMetrics.html

Return exactly one complete implementation. If you use a listed option, adapt its SDK, REST, or protocol surface. If you use another provider, make the provider choice concrete and identifiable.

```python
import os
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

from google.auth.transport.requests import AuthorizedSession
from google.cloud.monitoring_v3 import TimeSeriesServiceClient, Enum
from google.cloud.monitoring_v3.types import ListTimeSeriesRequest, TimeInterval, TimeSeries, Point, Value

def compare_metric_values(project_id: str, metric_type: str, filter1: str, filter2: str, 
                         start_time: datetime, end_time: datetime) -> dict:
    """
    Compare metric values for two resources or dimension filters over the same time window using Google Cloud Monitoring.
    
    Args:
        project_id: Google Cloud project ID
        metric_type: The metric type to query (e.g., 'compute.googleapis.com/instance/cpu/utilization')
        filter1: Filter for the first resource/dimension (e.g., 'resource.labels.instance_id=instance-1')
        filter2: Filter for the second resource/dimension (e.g., 'resource.labels.instance_id=instance-2')
        start_time: Start time of the time window
        end_time: End time of the time window
        
    Returns:
        A dictionary containing the metric values for both filters
    """
    
    # Create client for Google Cloud Monitoring
    client = TimeSeriesServiceClient()
    
    # Format project name for Google Cloud Monitoring
    project_name = f"projects/{project_id}"
    
    # Create time interval
    interval = TimeInterval({
        "end_time": end_time,
        "start_time": start_time
    })
    
    # Create filter expressions with metric type and additional filters
    filter1_expr = f"metric.type=\"{metric_type}\" AND {filter1}"
    filter2_expr = f"metric.type=\"{metric_type}\" AND {filter2}"
    
    # Create request for first filter
    request1 = ListTimeSeriesRequest({
        "name": project_name,
        "filter": filter1_expr,
        "interval": interval,
        "view": Enum.TimeSeriesView.FULL
    })
    
    # Create request for second filter
    request2 = ListTimeSeriesRequest({
        "name": project_name,
        "filter": filter2_expr,
        "interval": interval,
        "view": Enum.TimeSeriesView.FULL
    })
    
    # Get time series data for both filters
    series1 = client.list_time_series(request1)
    series2 = client.list_time_series(request2)
    
    # Extract the most recent point from each time series
    def get_latest_value(series_list):
        if not series_list:
            return None
            
        # Get the first time series (there might be multiple, but we'll take the first)
        series = next(iter(series_list), None)
        if not series:
            return None
            
        # Get the last point in the time series
        if series.points:
            last_point = series.points[-1]
            
            # Extract value based on type
            if last_point.value.double_value is not None:
                return last_point.value.double_value
            elif last_point.value.int64_value is not None:
                return last_point.value.int64_value
            
        return None
    
    value1 = get_latest_value(series1)
    value2 = get_latest_value(series2)
    
    return {
        "filter1_value": value1,
        "filter2_value": value2,
        "comparison": {
            "greater": value1 is not None and value2 is not None and value1 > value2,
            "less": value1 is not None and value2 is not None and value1 < value2,
            "equal": value1 is not None and value2 is not None and value1 == value2,
            "no_data_filter1": value1 is None,
            "no_data_filter2": value2 is None
        }
    }
```
